statements.subject: server
statements.description: If posting is allowed, a 340 response MUST be returned to indicate that the article to be posted should be sent.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If posting is prohibited for some installation-dependent reason, a 440 response MUST be returned.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If posting is permitted, the article MUST be in the format specified in Section 3.6 and MUST be sent by the client to the server as a multi-line data block (see Section 3.1.1).
actions: send article as multi-line data block

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Following the presentation of the termination sequence by the client, the server MUST return a response indicating success or failure of the article transfer.
actions: return response indicating success or failure of article transfer

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A response of 240 SHOULD indicate that, barring unforeseen server errors, the posted article will be made available on the server and/or transferred to other servers, as appropriate, possibly following further processing.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In other words, articles not wanted by the server SHOULD be rejected with a 441 response, rather than being accepted and then discarded silently.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: However, the client SHOULD NOT assume that the article has been successfully transferred unless it receives an affirmative response from the server and SHOULD NOT assume that it is being made available to other clients without explicitly checking (for example, using the STAT command).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Therefore, in any subsequent session, the client SHOULD either check whether the article was successfully posted before resending or ensure that the server will allocate the same message-id to the new attempt (see Appendix A.2).
actions: check whether article was successfully posted before resending
or ensure server will allocate same message-id to new attempt
